messages.author: f1f3f101bca43ab0
messages.subject: partially colored background.
parts:
Hi people!

I have got a graphic that shows the degree of efficiency of government
spending in education with geom_line (three lines actually). This
graphic represents the period from 1995 yo 2008. From 1998 and on
there is a new legislation. I would like to color the background (or
'front-ground' with alpha to make it very transparent, which would be
better, I think) from 1998 to 2008 to represents this scenario change.
I have tried it with geom_bar with no success. Any help?

Thanx.

Here is my reproducible example without the background or front-
ground.

malmacum<-structure(list(Ano = c(1995L, 1996L, 1997L, 1998L, 1999L,
2000L,
2001L, 2002L, 2003L, 2004L, 2005L, 2006L, 2007L, 2008L, 1995L,
1996L, 1997L, 1998L, 1999L, 2000L, 2001L, 2002L, 2003L, 2004L,
2005L, 2006L, 2007L, 2008L, 1995L, 1996L, 1997L, 1998L, 1999L,
2000L, 2001L, 2002L, 2003L, 2004L, 2005L, 2006L, 2007L, 2008L
), Indices = c(1, 1.071520963, 1.084394613, 1.044964539, 0.967453133,
0.930567334, 0.909193271, 0.911871081, 0.92011399, 0.892187372,
0.878773797, 0.861206621, 0.815263831, 0.749724319, 1, 0.993618333,
1.00075991, 1.012954837, 1.010809736, 1.009157923, 1.011221987,
1.019851475, 1.02240896, 1.025420106, 1.020497672, 1.019839186,
1.022533828, 1.01100813, 1, 1.078495259, 1.083658296, 1.031626402,
0.957094452, 0.922164829, 0.899153128, 0.894227117, 0.900084669,
0.870214893, 0.861241881, 0.844580902, 0.7974592, 0.741595411
), Malmquist = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L,
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L,
2L), .Label = c("Evolução da Eficiência Técnica", "Mudança
Tecnológica",
"Produtividade Total dos Fatores"), class = "factor")), .Names =
c("Ano",
"Indices", "Malmquist"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-42L))

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(malmacum, aes(x=Ano, y=Indices,
group=Malmquist,
colour=Malmquist,
shape=Malmquist))+
geom_line(size=0.8, alpha=0.8)+
geom_point(size=2.2)+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'),
axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'))+
theme_gray(base_size = 9)

p

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: partially colored background.
parts:
hi

probably there are several ways to do so, for example,

p<-ggplot(malmacum, aes(x=Ano, y=Indices,
group=Malmquist,
colour=Malmquist,
shape=Malmquist))+
geom_rect(aes(xmin=1998, xmax=2008, ymin=0.7, ymax=1.1, colour=NULL),
fill="red",alpha=0.005)+

geom_line(size=0.8, alpha=0.8)+
geom_point(size=2.2)+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'),
axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 8, colour = 'grey40'))+
theme_gray(base_size = 9)

print(p)

--
Kohske Takahashi <takahash...@gmail.com>

Research Center for Advanced Science and Technology,
The University of  Tokyo, Japan.
http://www.fennel.rcast.u-tokyo.ac.jp/profilee_ktakahashi.html
